_README.purpose: The conditions Pona can check, and the ingredients that trigger them.
_README.SCOPE_RULE: Pona answers exactly one question: 'does this food contain something I personally react to?' It does NOT rate food as healthy or unhealthy, and it does not give dietary advice for managing a disease. An entry qualifies only if ALL of: (1) it is a reaction to a specific identifiable INGREDIENT, never a food category like 'red meat' or 'fried food'; (2) the mechanism is supported by scientific evidence and reflected in food-regulator guidance; (3) stating it does not require judging the food itself.

REMOVED_AND_WHY.MSG sensitivity: The reported symptom cluster originates in a 1968 anecdote and has not been reproduced in controlled double-blind trials. FDA classifies MSG as generally recognized as safe. Asserting the effect would spread a claim the evidence does not support, and the original framing carries a well-documented racist history.
REMOVED_AND_WHY.Gout: Dietary management of a diagnosed disease, not an ingredient sensitivity, and it worked by flagging broad categories ('red meat', 'organ meat'). Genetics drive urate far more than diet does. Out of scope.
REMOVED_AND_WHY.GERD default trigger list: Reflux triggers are highly individual and current guidance favours identifying your own triggers over avoiding foods as a group. The condition remains, with the user supplying their own triggers.

_README.STATUS: SEED DATA - NOT CLINICALLY REVIEWED. This file governs allergen safety decisions and must be reviewed by a qualified dietitian or allergist before any real user relies on it.
_README.SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: This file is hand-curated source, not a generated artifact. notebooks/run_analysis.py reads it; nothing regenerates it.

Peanut allergy.explanation: Contains peanuts. Peanut is an FDA major allergen and reactions can be severe.

Tree nut allergy.explanation: Contains tree nuts. Tree nuts are an FDA major allergen and reactions can be severe.

Milk/Dairy allergy.explanation: Contains milk protein. This is an immune reaction to the protein, which is different from lactose intolerance.

Egg allergy.explanation: Contains egg. Egg is an FDA major allergen.

Fish allergy.explanation: Contains fish. Fish is an FDA major allergen and is often lifelong.

Shellfish allergy.explanation: Contains crustacean shellfish. This is an FDA major allergen and reactions can be severe.

Soy allergy.explanation: Contains soy. Soy is an FDA major allergen.

Sesame allergy.explanation: Contains sesame. Sesame became the 9th FDA major allergen in 2023 and must now be declared on US labels.

Wheat allergy.explanation: Contains wheat. Wheat is an FDA major allergen. This is an allergy to wheat protein, which is distinct from celiac disease.

Celiac disease.explanation: Contains gluten. Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition, not an allergy or an intolerance, and it requires strict avoidance of wheat, barley and rye.
Celiac disease.note: The FDA 'gluten-free' label means under 20 parts per million.

Lactose intolerance.explanation: Contains lactose. Lactose intolerance is dose-dependent, so the amount matters and many people tolerate some lactose without difficulty.
Lactose intolerance.prevalence: ~65% of the global population has reduced lactase persistence
Lactose intolerance.note: Not an allergy. Aged cheese and yogurt are lower in lactose and are often tolerated.

Sulfite sensitivity.explanation: Contains sulfites. The FDA requires sulfites to be declared at 10 parts per million or above because they can provoke asthma symptoms in some people with asthma.

Acid reflux / GERD.explanation: Reflux triggers differ a lot from person to person.
Acid reflux / GERD.note: Pona does not assume a trigger list for reflux. Current guidance favours identifying your own triggers over avoiding foods as a group. Add the foods you personally react to and Pona will watch for those. Things some people report reacting to include coffee, chocolate, citrus, tomato, mint and alcohol - but this varies, and it may not apply to you.
